title: Organisation & Sub‑Levels 📂
description: Keep large levels tidy with folders, layers, and level streaming.

slides.title: World Outliner Folders 🗂️
slides.content:
# Organise Your Actors

In Chapter 2 you learned the World Outliner shows all actors. Now go deeper:

* Click the **folder icon** to create a new folder.
* Drag actors into it.
* Folders can be nested (e.g., `Building → Interior → Furniture`).
* Use the eye icon to hide an entire folder.
* Folders don’t affect the hierarchy; they are purely visual organisation.

*Analogy:* Folders are like **drawers in a filing cabinet** – they group related items so you can find them quickly.

quizData.question: Putting actors into a World Outliner folder changes their parent‑child relationship.
quizData.explanation: Folders are for visual organisation only. Parenting is done by dragging actors onto each other, not into folders.

slides.title: Layers Panel 🎚️
slides.content:
## Quick Visibility Toggles

Open **Window → Layers** to see the Layers panel. Layers let you:

* Assign actors to named layers (e.g., `Lighting`, `Enemies`, `Props`)
* Toggle visibility of entire layers with one click
* Lock layers to prevent editing

Unlike folders, layers can contain actors from anywhere in the Outliner hierarchy. Use layers for **cross‑section visibility** – e.g., hide all foliage to see the underlying terrain.

slides.title: Sub‑Levels & Level Streaming 🌊
slides.content:
## Divide and Conquer

Large games don’t use a single massive level. Instead, they use **Level Streaming** – loading/unloading sub‑levels on demand.

* **Persistent Level** – the main level (always loaded)
* **Sub‑Levels** – separate level files that can be loaded/unloaded via Blueprints or volume triggers.

Benefits:
* Multiple designers can work on different sub‑levels simultaneously.
* Improve performance by only loading what’s near the player.
* Reuse sub‑levels across different persistent levels.

To add a sub‑level: **Levels** dropdown → **Add Existing** or **Create New**.

quizData.question: What is the benefit of using sub‑levels?

options.text: They make the level file smaller
They allow collaborative work and better performance

quizData.explanation: Sub‑levels enable team collaboration, streaming for performance, and reusability.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Levels Window Mastery

Use the **Levels** window (Window → Levels) to see all sub‑levels, toggle visibility, lock editing, and set streaming method. Right‑click a sub‑level → **Change Streaming Method** to Blueprint or Always Loaded.
